title: Super Ugly Number
summary: Identify the n-th super ugly number, defined as a positive integer with prime factors from the given array primes.
statement: Identify the n-th super ugly number, defined as a positive integer with prime factors from the given array primes. Provide the result as a 32-bit signed integer.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. primes contains 1–100 distinct ascending primes from 2 through 1000.
The nth result fits a signed 32-bit integer. The sequence starts with 1; each distinct integer is counted once.
hints: Every value after 1 is a listed prime multiplied by an earlier valid value.
Merge one increasing product stream per prime and suppress equal candidates.
Start values=[1]. Append the minimum p[i]*values[index[i]], then advance EVERY matching index.
Keep k stream positions and k candidate values. After n-1 appends, return the last value.
editorial: For each prime p, maintain its smallest product with a generated value that has not been emitted. The minimum across these streams is the next valid integer: dividing any candidate by one allowed prime reaches a smaller generated value. Advance all streams tied at the minimum so values remain distinct. This generalizes the fixed 2/3/5 problem to an input prime set. The independent oracle explores products with a heap and a global visited set.

tests.explanation: The sequence begins 1,2,4,7,8,13,14,16,19,26,28,32; the twelfth value is 32.
1 has no prime factors and is the first valid number for every allowed prime list.
